description: A 4-member crew of beginner builders and problem-solvers excited to innovate and tackle space challenges together.
summary: Our project is a beginner-level software prototype developed in alignment with the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. It aims to demonstrate how astronauts' basic health parameters can be monitored and evaluated during space missions. The system generates simulated health data using threshold values obtained from NASA-related reference data and applies conditional logic to determine whether the readings fall within acceptable ranges. A user-friendly interface, developed using Streamlit, displays the generated readings and their evaluation results. The system also produces a health status report, providing a simple overview of the astronaut's monitored health parameters.
details:
Project Summary

The project uses a random data generation module to simulate astronaut health readings. These readings are generated within predefined ranges using threshold values referenced from NASA-related health data. Since this is an introductory prototype, simulated data is used instead of actual readings collected from astronauts or wearable medical devices.

A conditional evaluation mechanism processes the generated readings by comparing them against the predefined threshold values. Based on these comparisons, the system identifies whether individual health parameters fall within their specified acceptable ranges or require attention. This demonstrates the fundamental logic behind automated health monitoring and alert-based evaluation systems.

For data presentation, we developed a Streamlit-based graphical user interface (GUI) that allows users to interact with the monitoring system and view the generated health information in an organized and accessible format. The interface displays the simulated readings along with their corresponding evaluation results, making it easier to understand the astronaut's current simulated health status.

Additionally, the system generates a health status report that summarizes the evaluated parameters and provides an overall overview of the astronaut's simulated health condition. This report demonstrates how health information can be organized into a readable format to support monitoring and preliminary assessment.

Overall, our project serves as an initial exploration of software-assisted astronaut health monitoring. Although it is currently limited to simulated data and basic threshold-based evaluation, it establishes a foundation for future improvements, such as integration with real-time wearable sensors, historical health-data tracking, graphical trend analysis, more advanced anomaly detection, and automated alerts. Our primary objective is to demonstrate the basic working principles of a digital astronaut health monitoring system while developing our understanding of programming, data processing, and user-interface development.
